summary: The post-census boundary recorded the four wheel-corner rows (corner_fl/fr/rl/rr) refusing typed at 'the wheel-frame non-z revolve'. This packet lands the recorded revolve-axis frame carrier: the door's `revolve(shape, axis, revolution_arc)` now records an expressible non-z axis (build123d `Axis` or a `Vector` direction) in the same local `(radius >= 0, axial)` revolve-plane convention as today's z-lathe, and emits the landed frame row carrying the axis as a full orthonormal placement (`world = translate(o) ∘ R ∘ M`, local z to the recorded axis direction). Volume is invariant under R (exact, never recomputed); the world bbox is the AABB of the 8 rotated local corners; the mesh transforms per vertex. The legacy z-axis path keeps its recorded row shape byte-for-byte (the existing z-revolve regression net is untouched). A zero/degenerate axis refuses typed (`DegenerateRevolveAxis`); a profile that is not a single-sided meridian generator about the axis (a point folding across the axis, a profile lying on the axis, or an axis parallel to its profile ray) refuses typed naming the gap. The four named kernel-door corner rows now pass the wheel-frame axle revolve and refuse typed at the NEXT boundary (a boolean subtract). Three named kernel tests are green: the non-z axle revolve answers exact world facts (volume equals the exact lathe volume of the same ring, world bbox equals the rotated ring bbox); the z-axis rows answer bit-identically with the legacy row shape and exact lathe facts; and an unsupported (degenerate) axis refuses typed naming `DegenerateRevolveAxis`.

implementation.door_recording: corpus/ttc/door.py: `revolve` now resolves the axis direction (build123d `Axis` or `Vector`) into a unit vector, records the legacy z profile unchanged when the unit is +z, and otherwise expresses the recorded profile in the local `(radius >= 0, axial)` revolve-plane coordinates of the axis through the frame origin plus the full orthonormal frame (x_dir = the profile's reference ray, z_dir = the axis unit, fixed-order completion for y). Radius is recorded as the non-negative in-plane coordinate along the single-sided reference ray, never a folded magnitude or a silently normalized zero. Partial arcs, non-Face shapes, open profiles, spline profiles with interpolation options, and the legacy outside-the-y=0-plane profiles keep their typed refusals unchanged. Helper functions `_axis_unit`, `_legacy_z_profile`, `_axis_profile`, `_axis_ray`, `_axis_perp`, `_axis_point`, and `_axis_frame` are pure client-side data transforms.
implementation.bridge_and_kernel: truck123d/src/bd_bridge.rs: no functional kernel change was required (the landed PartSpec `rotation` frame already answers a z-lathe placed under an arbitrary orthonormal frame with exact volume invariance, rotated-corner world bbox, and per-vertex mesh transforms). The three required kernel tests were added in the in-crate tests: they build revolve rows through the corpus door python (pure client data), parse them with `parse_tree`, and measure exact world facts with `tree_facts`.
implementation.kernel_tests: Three tests added in truck123d/src/bd_bridge.rs mod tests: revolve_about_nonz_axis_answers_world_facts (a ring revolved about the wheel-frame axle, world volume = exact lathe volume, world bbox = the rotated ring bbox), z_revolve_rows_answer_bit_identically (the z-axis path records the legacy row with no frame and exact analytic lathe facts), and revolve_refuses_unsupported_axes_typed (a zero-length axis refuses typed naming DegenerateRevolveAxis).

findings.title: The mvac-style refusal-battery pin for an axis-aligned non-z revolve now moves (admitted), not refused
findings.detail: tests/ttc_lathe_spline.rs `revolve_refusals_stay_typed_after_spline_admission`'s `non_z_axis` sub-case revolves a closed rect ring about the X axis through the origin. Under FRAME-REVOLVE that revolve is an expressible recorded carrier (identical in kind to the census axle revolves), so the door no longer refuses it - the typed refusal surface moved to genuinely unsupported forms (degenerate axis / non-meridian profile). This is the same pin-movement class as the mvac pin, which the orchestrator adjudicated separately after the frame-carrier cure; the test file is outside this packet's write scope. No other pin in the crate moved.
findings.evidence: The mvac/nozzle/spline z-regression pins all stay green; the four corner census rows now deepen to the boolean-subtract typed refusal recorded above.

stop_conditions.spec_gap: No SPEC_GAP: the placement composition expresses the axle revolve exactly (volume invariant under R by construction; world bbox and mesh re-derived from the recorded frame, exactly as the frame policy fixes).
stop_conditions.verdict_neutral: No defect record: every existing green z-revolve row answers identically (mvac, nozzle, spline shell pins green; z-lathe facts bit-identical), no recorded reference file changed, and only the intended non-z typed-refusal pin moved (adjudication item F1, mvac style). The pre-existing pb_parity monocoque OCC-baseline environment failure is base parity.
